Issue 2.summary: Auric’s exhausted residents are already turning against refugees when a mixed Verge–Shard evacuation ship arrives under fire, forcing Halev to spend his government on people he cannot house.
Issue 2.settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — REFUGEE BERTH AND CIVIC DOCK — NIGHT
panelPlan: Wide: Auric’s beautiful market ring is dimmed by rationing; displaced families sleep beneath shuttered stalls while residents argue across a portable heater queue.
The Luminara Mother gives the Boy her place near the heater as Wallace shows Halev a petition demanding the refugee berth be closed.
Jex interrupts with a broken distress transmission: an unscheduled evacuation ship, carrying both Verge and Shard civilians, is approaching inside the supply convoy.
Wallace warns there are no beds, heat reserves, or votes for this; through the canopy, distant weapons fire flashes around the crippled ship.
Halev orders the berth opened. Dock crews move while Wallace quietly says this may end Halev’s government; Halev watches the ship burn toward them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: Closer to the heater. I’m not asking twice.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: So are nine thousand voters, and they want this berth closed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: They may have to shout. We have an unscheduled ship coming in loud.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: People. Verge and Shard. Several hundred, if the life signs are honest.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: That may be the last order this government obeys.

directionInline: Enter on Auric’s refugee berth already at its moral limit: the Mother protects the Boy while residents blame displaced families for the cold. Wallace brings Halev the political price of admitting anyone else. The scene turns when Jex’s distress feed reveals that the expected supply operation now includes a burning ship of mixed Verge and Shard evacuees. Halev cannot promise beds or heat, only entry; he opens the berth despite Wallace’s warning. Exit on dock crews running toward the airlocks as the damaged ship appears under fire beyond the canopy.

Issue 2.summary: Inside the crippled evacuation ship, Dr. Richard Secundo abandons the bridge to keep a mixed group of enemies alive while his son Paul inherits control of a vessel coming apart.
Issue 2.settingText: EVACUATION FREIGHTER MERCY OF DAWN — PASSENGER HOLD
panelPlan: Hundreds of Verge and Shard civilians pack a freight hold as a pressure door bows inward; adults from both factions brace it with cargo poles and their bodies.
Richard treats a wounded Shard caregiver who pushes their last oxygen mask toward a frightened Verge child.
Paul reports from an exposed engineering crawl that the bridge can retain pressure or the passenger hold can—there is not enough power for both.
Richard looks toward the distant bridge, then orders Paul to vent it and transfer control to his repair slate; he is terrified and obeys.
The lights stabilize for one breath. Cutting torches ignite on the outer hull beside the children; Richard tells Paul to keep them moving.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Keep pressure on that brace. Together—don’t match uniforms, match hands.

dialogueInline.speaker: Shard Caregiver
dialogueInline.text: Give the mask to the kid.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Dad, the bridge is pulling our reserve. I can’t hold both sections.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Can you transfer helm to engineering?

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: That isn’t a helm. It’s my repair slate.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Tonight it’s a helm. Vent the bridge.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: There could still be people up there.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: I checked. Paul—look at me. Save the room that answers.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Control transferred. Something’s cutting through the hull.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Then keep us moving while I meet it.

directionInline: Enter with civilians physically holding their shared air inside a freighter whose faction lines are collapsing under necessity. Richard’s treatment of a wounded Shard caregiver shows mutual sacrifice before Paul presents the impossible engineering choice. The turn is Richard’s decision to abandon the empty bridge and place control in his frightened son’s hands. Pressure returns to the passenger hold, but the consequence is loss of the protected command section. Exit as raider torches flare against the hull and Richard turns from doctor to defender.

Issue 2.summary: Billie converts Abby’s cargo raid into a political atrocity, while Tess realizes grievance has become an excuse to punish civilians.
panelPlan: Through Ashfang’s canopy, supply containers separate from the crippled refugee ship; Abby’s order marks the containers while Billie marks the passenger hull.
Tess challenges the changed target over comm as boarding crews load weapons; Billie shows an old image of Shard families frozen outside a Fleet cordon.
Abby orders Billie back to cargo. Billie argues the mixed ship will expose Fleet mercy as selective and cuts Abby’s channel.
A raider hesitates at the boarding collar after hearing children through the hull; Billie personally slams the collar forward.
Ashfang bites into the passenger section while Gravefire turns away from the cargo prize and follows.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Containers only. Leave the passenger hull.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: They left ours outside the cordon.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: No. They just learned whose suffering gets a cruiser.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: This is not the target. Break off.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: It’s the only target anyone will remember.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raider
dialogueInline.text: I hear children through the plate.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: I listened when ours froze. Clamp us in.

directionInline: Enter with Abby’s limited cargo raid still recoverable, then let Billie redirect it toward the refugee hull for explicitly political reasons. Tess confronts the pain beneath Billie’s choice without accepting what she is doing with it; Abby’s authority fails when Billie cuts the channel. The turn comes when even Billie’s raider hears children and hesitates, but Billie drives the boarding collar home herself. The consequence is a public breach between captains. Exit with Gravefire abandoning the profitable target to pursue Ashfang.

Issue 2.summary: Ordered to protect authorized cargo and treat the refugees as a threat, Venn knowingly trades her command for the burning ship.
panelPlan: Thunderbreak’s luminous bridge shows two crises: exposed medicine and heater cargo on one side, the refugee freighter being boarded on the other.
Dominion appears by holo and orders Venn to hold the authorized supply screen; the mixed evacuees are labeled an infiltration risk.
Tactical explains that diverting leaves Auric’s supplies open. The officer quietly tells Venn Dominion’s order is logged.
Venn asks the bridge to identify anyone receiving the refugee distress call; every station light answers. She orders the turn.
Exterior: Thunderbreak leaves the cargo screen and dives through wreckage toward Mercy of Dawn as raider fire begins walking across its hull.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Your authorization covers supplies, not unidentified passengers.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Alongside Shard codes. Hold your screen.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: If we divert, the medicine convoy is exposed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Is anyone on this bridge unable to hear their distress call?

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Auric, protect the cargo if you can. Thunderbreak is going for the people.

directionInline: Enter with Thunderbreak able to protect either Auric’s desperately needed supplies or the unauthorized refugee ship. Dominion makes the political danger explicit and labels mixed civilians a security risk; Venn’s own officers make sure she understands the material and career costs. The turn is not a tactical insight but her question about who can hear the distress call. She disobeys in full view of her crew. Exit on the massive cruiser abandoning the safe formation and diving toward people it has been ordered to distrust.

Issue 2.summary: Naomi prevents Fleet rescue from becoming Fleet occupation, and Venn proves trust by surrendering control when command would be easier.
Issue 2.settingText: VERGE ESCORT — COCKPIT / THUNDERBREAK RESCUE BAY
panelPlan: Naomi sees Fleet marines loading in Thunderbreak’s rescue bay while Richard’s broken transmission identifies frightened Shard and Verge families together.
Naomi tells Venn armed Fleet control will make half the ship resist rescue; Venn argues that waiting will kill them all.
Naomi’s second receives a voice fragment from a parent aboard and asks Naomi not to let strangers take the ship.
Naomi demands operational lead and Verge markings on the first shuttle. Venn removes her own officer from the lead seat and grants it publicly.
A small shuttle carrying Naomi, Verge crew, Fleet medics, and unraised weapons launches into fire; Venn remains behind, answerable for Naomi’s choices.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Mercy of Dawn to anyone—boarders are inside the outer skin.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: My rescue team launches in forty seconds.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Not with rifles first. They’ll think you came to take the ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Captain, in forty seconds there may be no ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: Second
dialogueInline.text: That was my father on the open channel.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Then we go. Verge lead, Fleet medics, weapons down.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Then your officer can explain the uniforms while the doors stay locked.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Officer, give Captain Sol the seat.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: That was an order—and a trust. Launch.

directionInline: Enter with Venn moving decisively toward a rescue that the refugees may experience as seizure. Naomi fights her over who gets to enter armed, and her second’s parent on the distress call makes distrust personal rather than ideological. The turn comes when Naomi demands lead authority and Venn relinquishes it publicly. The consequence is a mixed rescue team whose success now depends on Verge legitimacy and Fleet capability together. Exit on their shuttle flying toward the burning hull with weapons deliberately lowered.

Issue 2.summary: With one shuttle load left before the ship breaks, Naomi sends the children away and stays behind with the adults she cannot promise to save.
Issue 2.settingText: MERCY OF DAWN — FRACTURED PASSENGER HOLD
panelPlan: Naomi’s team enters a hold divided by a widening structural crack; one rescue shuttle remains docked while hundreds press toward it.
Richard explains the shuttle can carry the children or a smaller mixed group of injured adults, not both; the hull has minutes.
A Verge child refuses boarding without the wounded Shard caregiver who gave up an oxygen mask; panic threatens the transfer.
Naomi puts the caregiver aboard in her own place, gives command of the shuttle to a junior rescuer, and seals herself, Richard, Paul, and the remaining adults inside.
Through the closing window, children reach for parents as the shuttle departs. Naomi turns back to the failing compartment and asks who can still work.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: One load. Children fill it, or I choose which wounded adults live.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: You can if you’re carrying our children. Seal it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: All right. Who in this room can still use their hands?

directionInline: Enter on rescue becoming triage as the fractured hold offers only one remaining shuttle load. Richard states the choice cleanly; a child’s refusal to abandon the Shard caregiver turns categories into a relationship. Naomi gives up her own place, sends the children and caregiver, and stays with everyone the shuttle cannot take. The consequence is emotional separation through a closing hatch and Naomi stranded on a dying ship. Exit as she turns grief into collective action by asking the remaining adults to help save one another.

Issue 2.summary: Tess disables one of her own raiders to protect a refugee, then seals the breach beside Naomi as both women cross a faction line they cannot uncross.
Issue 2.settingText: MERCY OF DAWN — RAIDER BREACH / PASSENGER HOLD
panelPlan: Tess enters through Ashfang’s smoking breach and finds a raider tearing medical packs from Richard while the pressure patch fails behind them.
Tess orders the packs returned. The raider invokes Billie and raises a weapon toward a refugee who tries to intervene.
Tess strikes first, pinning and disarming her own crew member; Naomi arrives with her weapon trained on Tess.
The breach splits wider. Naomi and Tess lower their weapons simultaneously and brace a patch while Richard pulls civilians clear.
The seal holds. On Billie’s monitor, Tess is unmistakably visible working beside Naomi; Tess hears Billie call her traitor and does not release the patch.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Billie says many things near an audience.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: That case keeps twelve people breathing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: You expect me to trust you?

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: No. I expect you to notice the air leaving.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Gravefire, you are aiding the enemy.

directionInline: Enter on Tess discovering that Billie’s political performance has become ordinary predation inside the hold. Her own raider forces the conflict by threatening a civilian, and Tess disables him before Naomi arrives ready to treat her as another attacker. The breach widening turns mutual suspicion into a physical choice: both women lower their guns and hold the same pressure patch. The consequence is that Tess’s defection becomes visible to Billie. Exit with Tess refusing Billie’s accusation because releasing the plate would kill the people behind her.

Issue 2.summary: When the refugee ship splits from the supplies Auric needs to survive, Venn chooses the people in front of her and forces Halev to bear the people who may die later.
Issue 2.settingText: THUNDERBREAK — BRIDGE / AURIC CIVIC CONTROL / MERCY OF DAWN
panelPlan: Mercy of Dawn breaks into a passenger section and a supply spine as luminous debris closes; Thunderbreak’s single tractor field cannot hold both.
Naomi calls from the passenger hold while Richard supports failing patients; the tactical display counts hundreds of life signs there.
Halev appears beside Auric’s dark rings and names what is in the other section: heat for North Ring and antibiotics for the fever ward.
Venn refuses both Naomi’s demand and Halev’s arithmetic for one silent beat, then locks the tractor onto the passenger hull.
Thunderbreak pulls the people clear while the supply spine drifts toward debris. Halev orders Auric’s clinics to prepare for what will now be missing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: The spine is separating. One tractor field—one section.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: We have three hundred people back here. Take the hold.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: The other half carries heat for nine thousand and medicine for a fever ward.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: I have patients who will not survive another impact.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: And I have patients who will not survive the week.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Do not make the cargo sound like things.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: I won’t. Lock the passenger section.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Understood. Auric clinics, revise intake. We have just lost the next week.

directionInline: Enter at the moment the freighter physically divides the rescue into immediate and delayed deaths. Naomi and Richard plead for the visible passengers while Halev gives the supplies their human consequence. The turn is Venn’s refusal to hide behind arithmetic: she chooses the passenger section knowing the other choice also contains lives. Thunderbreak saves hundreds now, and Auric inherits a foreseeable medical and heating crisis. Exit on Halev beginning that grim preparation as the supply spine tumbles away.

Issue 2.summary: Jex gives up the hidden passage that made him powerful because a partial secret would send Tess and Auric’s supplies to their deaths.
Issue 2.settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — VEIL MARKET BACK ROOM
panelPlan: Jex watches the supply spine drift toward destruction on a route table while his private Veil passage glows beneath layers of locked seals.
Halev asks for the route; Jex names the clients, safe houses, and years of leverage that open transmission would expose.
Halev has nothing left to buy it with and asks whether Jex built roads to move people or traps to own them.
Jex offers only the first marker; the scribe calculates that Tess will enter blind and die at the second turn. Jex removes every seal.
The full passage erupts across public channels. Jex’s waiting clients destroy their route tokens as Tess turns toward the revealed path.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: You know a way to that spine.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: I know why no one else knows it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Every client who trusted me, three safe houses, and the only advantage I cannot replace.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: I have nothing left to offer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Did you build roads, Jex, or traps?

dialogueInline.speaker: Scribe
dialogueInline.text: Without the second turn, they enter the shear blind.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Of course they do. Open all of it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: You will never own that route again.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Then somebody had better live long enough to misuse it.

directionInline: Enter with Jex possessing the only path that can recover Auric’s supplies and Halev possessing nothing with which to purchase it. The route data is concrete navigation information—timing windows, shear markers, anchor fixes and the second turn needed to keep the ships inside the usable reciprocal gradient—not mystical secret knowledge. Jex first tries to surrender only enough information to retain control, but the scribe exposes that half a route is a death sentence. The turn is Jex stripping every seal himself. Exit on his priceless map becoming public while the people who trusted him erase their ties.

Issue 2.summary: Naomi and Tess carry the severed refugee ship and its supplies through a spectacular broken-moon passage while Paul must trust his father to disappear from view.
Issue 2.settingText: THE SHATTERWAKE — MULTI-LOCATION INTERCUT: REFUGEE PASSENGER HULL / SUPPLY SPINE / GRAVEFIRE / THUNDERBREAK
panelPlan: Panel 1 — exterior establishing shot; no faces or shared interior: luminous fragments of a shattered moon rotate inside a violet nebula. Naomi’s small Verge escort shepherds the severed passenger hull; Gravefire braces the loose supply spine; Thunderbreak stops at the passage mouth because the cruiser cannot fit.

Panel 2 — supply-spine engineering blister; Paul is the only physically present named character. He straps himself beside exposed machinery and steers from his repair slate. A small navigation display shows Naomi’s Verge escort beside the distant passenger hull. Dialogue in exact order: Naomi over bordered radio balloon, ‘Paul, bring our nose toward the blue fracture.’ Paul, ‘It keeps moving.’ Tess over a differently styled radio balloon, ‘Everything here moves. Pick the part moving slowest.’ Do not show Naomi, Tess, or Richard in this compartment.

Panel 3 — supply-spine engineering blister; Paul remains the only physically present named character. His small comm screen shows Richard working over patients inside the separate passenger-hull medical hold. Dialogue in exact order: Richard through the screen, ‘Paul, eyes on your slate.’ Paul, ‘I can’t see your section.’ Richard through the screen, ‘You do not need to see me to know I’m working.’ Rotating moon fragments eclipse the passenger hull, and Richard’s image breaks into static. Do not put Richard physically beside Paul.

Panel 4 — Thunderbreak bridge; Venn is the only physically present named character, framed against the passage the cruiser cannot enter. Dialogue in exact order: Venn, ‘Thunderbreak will not fit through.’ Naomi replies through a bordered radio balloon, ‘Then come around the long way.’ Venn, ‘I intend to.’ Do not show Naomi on Thunderbreak.

Panel 5 — Gravefire cockpit; Tess is the only physically present named character. A gravity pulse pulls the supply spine away as Tess drives Gravefire bodily against it. Dialogue in exact order: Tess, ‘Supply spine is slipping. I’m going to push it.’ Naomi answers through a bordered radio balloon, ‘That is not a tow.’ Tess, ‘It is if we survive it.’ Do not show Naomi inside Gravefire.

Panel 6 — exterior closing shot; no dialogue and no group portrait: Naomi’s escort and the passenger hull disappear through one luminous gap while Gravefire pushes the supply spine carrying Paul through another. Far behind them, Thunderbreak turns alone toward the pursuing raiders. The ships’ separation must be unmistakable.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Paul, bring our nose toward the blue fracture.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Everything here moves. Pick the part moving slowest.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: You do not need to see me to know I’m working.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Then come around the long way.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Supply spine is slipping. I’m going to push it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: It is if we survive it.

directionInline: Stage this as a six-panel multi-location intercut connected by radio, not as five people sharing one room. Paul is alone inside the supply spine’s improvised engineering blister, steering it from his repair slate. Richard is aboard the separate passenger hull, treating patients in its damaged medical hold. Naomi pilots her Verge escort alongside the passenger hull and calls course corrections to Paul over comms. Tess remains inside Gravefire while using her ship’s hull to push the supply spine. Venn remains on Thunderbreak’s bridge outside the passage and appears only in the dedicated Thunderbreak panel. Make the Shatterwake physically legible: rotating moon fragments and damaged corridor geometry shift the local reciprocal gradient; Naomi’s instruction to choose the slowest-moving fracture is an empirical way of choosing the least violent shear. Thunderbreak’s mass and field envelope cannot safely fit the usable gap. Never render a colorful hyperspace tunnel or mystical portal. The emotional line is Paul continuing to steer when the passenger hull carrying his father vanishes from view.

Issue 2.summary: Abby publicly chooses the refugees and her sister over Billie, splitting the Shards and turning a political disagreement into a broken intimate loyalty.
panelPlan: Ashfang lines up on Gravefire as it shoves the supply spine; Abby’s smaller skiff crosses between them while Shard captains watch on open comms.
Billie turns Tess’s rescue into a test of whether Abby will choose her sister over Shard unity; Abby refuses the framing and points to the civilians Tess protects.
Billie invokes everything she and Abby survived together and asks whether Venn matters more; Abby says the people Billie erased from consideration matter.
Billie advances. Abby fires across Ashfang’s bow, scorching its armor; the watching skiffs divide into two formations.
Ashfang withdraws behind its supporters. Tess continues into the passage without thanking Abby; Abby remains between both camps, having lost half her fleet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Tess chose people you were about to kill.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: I chose the people in front of me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Is Venn worth more than everything we survived?

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: This is not about Venn. It is about everyone you decided did not count.

directionInline: Enter with Billie about to punish Tess for rescuing the supply spine and Abby forced to take a visible side. Billie makes Tess’s rescue a test of whether Abby will choose her sister over Shard unity, then invokes her own history with Abby. Abby refuses both frames and returns the conflict to the civilians Billie erased. The turn is a real warning shot that damages Ashfang and divides the watching captains. Exit with Tess escaping, Billie taking half the skiffs, and Abby stranded inside the familial and political cost of her choice.

Issue 2.summary: Thunderbreak fights alone at the passage mouth, and Venn makes a frightened junior officer choose rescue over a clean act of revenge.
panelPlan: Epic exterior: Thunderbreak holds the narrow mouth against Billie’s skiffs, armor shining under impacts while refugee sections disappear behind it.
On the damaged bridge, Venn opens defensive drones like a luminous fan to bend missiles into rotating moon debris.
A junior officer finds a clean shot on a retreating Shard ship responsible for an earlier civilian strike and asks permission to take it.
The same power can fire or preserve the failing tractor field protecting the last passenger section. Venn makes the officer state who benefits from each choice.
The officer drops the solution and feeds the tractor. Thunderbreak takes a brutal hit, but the last civilian hull clears as bridge lights fail.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Three salvos inbound. Point defense is saturated.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Open the drones. Let the moon take them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: I have the cutter that hit the Luminara ship. Clean solution.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Who lives if you do not?

directionInline: Enter with Thunderbreak fighting a comprehensible holding action: it is the shield between pursuing skiffs and escaping people. The battle is gorgeous but every device serves the human objective. A junior officer receives a justified chance at revenge, then learns firing would consume the power keeping civilians alive. The turn belongs to the officer when they abandon the kill and feed the tractor. The consequence is severe damage to Thunderbreak. Exit in darkness as the last refugee hull slips beyond the cruiser.

Issue 2.summary: Auric residents try to divide the arrivals by faction until the Luminara Mother gives part of her own berth to the Shard caregiver who saved a Verge child.
panelPlan: The severed passenger hull opens into an overwhelmed concourse; wounded Verge and Shard families emerge together beneath improvised faction barriers.
Residents demand that Shard arrivals be searched and separated. Wallace tells Halev the crowd will not accept them in the existing berth.
Richard refuses to let medics split mixed family and care groups; the wounded Shard caregiver arrives beside the Verge child saved earlier.
The Luminara Mother recognizes what happened, removes a barrier herself, and offers half of her family’s tiny berth to the caregiver.
Others begin moving barriers while some residents turn away in anger. Halev orders all faction partitions removed and accepts the unrest.

dialogueInline.speaker: Resident
dialogueInline.text: Shard side stays behind the red line.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: There is no Shard side. These are my patients.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: It is already deciding what kind of place this is.

dialogueInline.speaker: Shard Caregiver
dialogueInline.text: Two. If my sister made it off.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: We have one berth and too much floor. Take half.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: One gesture will not house hundreds.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: Start with the one in your hand.

directionInline: Enter on rescued civilians reaching safety only to encounter faction barriers inside it. Richard fights the attempt to separate patients, while Wallace turns public anger into political pressure. The turn comes when the child identifies the Shard caregiver as the person who shared oxygen, and the Mother sacrifices scarce private space rather than offering abstract tolerance. The gesture does not solve capacity, but it changes what refusal looks like. Exit with Halev ordering the partitions removed as both solidarity and backlash spread.

Issue 2.summary: Dominion offers Venn her command in exchange for separating Shard refugees from their families; she refuses and removes her insignia before her crew.
panelPlan: Emergency lamps illuminate Thunderbreak’s scarred bridge while Auric receives mixed families; Dominion and Keating appear over a fractured holo table.
Dominion orders all Shard arrivals detained and Naomi’s rescuers surrendered for questioning, presenting compliance as the only way to preserve Fleet relief.
Venn asks whether children and mixed households will be separated. Keating says classification is not punishment; an officer reacts despite trying not to.
Dominion privately offers Venn continued command if she executes the order. Venn removes her star insignia and sets it beside the damaged route display.
The holo vanishes. Some crew salute; others stare at dead consoles and the stranded cruiser, frightened by the cost of following her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Detain every Shard arrival. Verge nationals may disembark after screening.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: It is when the door locks.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Captain Sol’s rescuers will also submit to inquiry.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: They just brought the children through.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Ella. Carry this out and you retain command.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Then you have made the price very clear. No.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Officer, record that Commodore Venn declines the order and yields command pending tribunal.

directionInline: Enter on Thunderbreak damaged but victorious while Fleet leadership turns rescue into classification and control. Dominion and Keating make the bargain concrete: Venn can preserve her command and Auric’s relief only by separating the people she saved. The bridge crew’s breach of protocol shows the order has become personal. The turn is Dominion’s private offer and Venn’s quiet refusal. She removes her insignia rather than forcing the institution to perform the gesture. Exit on a divided crew confronting the material danger her moral decision has left them in.

Issue 2.summary: Unable to house the refugees without breaking mixed families, Halev opens Auric’s unsafe luxury ring and makes enemies of the traders who kept him in power.
panelPlan: Halev, Wallace, Richard, and Paul stand before the sealed Crown Ring: elegant empty apartments curve around a spectacular cracked observation window while refugees crowd outside.
Wallace explains that the ring is structurally suspect and its suites hold bonded goods belonging to the traders who support Halev’s coalition.
Richard rejects the alternative allocation plan because it separates mixed households and care groups; Paul finds the fracture monitors are old but responsive.
Halev orders the stored luxuries removed and families admitted under continuous watch. Wallace tells him the owners will bring down the government.
Doors open onto the gorgeous failing habitat. Refugees enter carrying almost nothing as repair crews—including Paul—move toward the glowing crack.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: The Crown Ring is sealed for a reason.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Two reasons. One is the window. The other is rich people’s furniture.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Your allocation splits twelve families and every care group from the ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: The fracture monitors still answer. Barely.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Can we watch the glass continuously?

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Clear the bonded stores. Move the families together.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Then they can finance somewhere else to sleep.

directionInline: Enter at Auric’s last available shelter, a breathtaking luxury ring kept empty by structural danger and private influence. Wallace makes both risks real while Richard refuses an efficient plan that would break the relationships keeping traumatized people alive. The turn comes when Paul confirms the ring can be inhabited only through constant human vigilance. Halev opens it and sacrifices his coalition rather than divide the refugees. Exit with displaced families entering beauty built for the powerful while Paul joins the repair watch.

Issue 2.summary: Naomi accuses Venn of making a heroic rescue whose aftermath the Verge must carry; their partnership survives only after Venn stops defending herself.
Issue 2.settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — SERVICE AIRLOCK OVERLOOKING THUNDERBREAK
panelPlan: Naomi finds Venn alone in a service airlock, watching damaged Thunderbreak beyond Auric’s glass while refugee traffic moves behind them.
Naomi lists the consequences landing on Auric: lost Fleet relief, divided residents, exposed defenses, and hundreds with nowhere durable to live.
Venn begins to explain the rescue; Naomi stops her and asks whether the Fleet always leaves after making itself the hero.
Venn admits Naomi is right and reveals she may no longer control Thunderbreak tomorrow; she offers defensive codes rather than another promise.
Naomi sets strict terms—Verge command, civilian oversight, no permanent Fleet presence. Venn accepts, and they turn together toward the work.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: You saved them. Now my docks have no relief, no room, and half a Shard fleet looking for an answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: No. You can leave. Knowing is what the rest of us do after you go.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Will Thunderbreak still be yours tomorrow?

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Probably not. Tonight I can give you her defensive codes and every working drone.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Verge command. Civilian oversight. No Fleet base hidden inside the gift.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: I would distrust you if you weren’t.

directionInline: Enter with Naomi refusing to let the damaged cruiser make Venn’s sacrifice the only visible cost. She names the aftermath the Verge cannot fly away from, and Venn’s instinct to explain nearly repeats the imbalance between them. The turn comes when Venn accepts the accusation without defending her intentions. Because she offers capability without control, Naomi can set terms that protect Verge sovereignty. Exit with anger intact but trust strong enough to survive it, both women facing the same crisis.

Issue 2.summary: Billie takes a civilian tug hostage and demands Tess, forcing Abby to choose openly between her sister and the unity of the Shards.
Issue 2.settingText: AURIC APPROACH — REFUGEE SERVICE TUG / SHARD COMMS
panelPlan: Ashfang clamps a civilian service tug carrying repair workers and oxygen cylinders beside the inhabited Crown Ring; Billie broadcasts across Auric.
Paul, aboard after joining the window repair crew, hides beneath machinery and reports that Billie has begun bleeding atmosphere.
Billie demands Tess surrender, arguing that Abby must choose her traitorous sister or the Shards she claims to lead.
Tess prepares to launch alone. Abby physically blocks Gravefire’s hatch and tells her dying for Billie will not save the hostages.
Billie opens a vent valve remotely. Frost blooms across the tug windows as Abby orders every captain still loyal to her to attack Ashfang.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Auric, I found the flaw in your open door.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Dad—if you hear this, I’m on the service tug. We’re losing air.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Send me Tess and I give back what’s left.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: She's baiting you. Dying for it won't help anyone.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Choose, Abby. Your sister or your people.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Tess is my people. So are the ones you are venting.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: You could lose every captain you have left.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Then I chose badly before today.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: All ships still taking my orders—target Ashfang.

directionInline: Enter with Billie turning Auric’s fragile hospitality into a hostage spectacle and placing Paul inside the danger so the threat reaches Richard personally. Her demand exploits the fact that Abby and Tess are sisters, framing family loyalty as betrayal of the Shards. Tess tries to sacrifice herself, but Abby recognizes that Billie wants submission, not exchange. The turn is Abby naming both Tess and the hostages as her people. Exit as atmosphere crystals across the tug windows and Abby’s divided fleet moves.

Issue 2.summary: Fleet, Verge, and rebel Shard rescuers save the hostage tug together while Abby defeats Billie but chooses civilian lives over revenge.
Issue 2.settingText: AURIC CROWN RING — HOSTAGE TUG / ASHFANG BATTLESPACE
panelPlan: Full-energy opening: Ashfang fires past Abby’s skiffs toward the hostage tug; crippled Thunderbreak rolls between the shot and Auric’s luminous Crown Ring.
Naomi grapples the venting tug with her escort while Paul crawls through freezing machinery to reach the manual valve.
Tess breaches Ashfang’s boarding collar and cuts the remote vent control; Billie attacks her inside the narrow industrial passage.
Abby disables Ashfang’s firing assembly and has Billie’s escape pod in her sights, but Naomi calls that the tug is tearing free with people aboard.
Abby abandons the shot and braces the tug beside Naomi. Billie escapes; Paul closes the valve, and mixed civilians pull one another toward returning air.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Paul, the manual valve is aft of the oxygen rack.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Then stay beneath it. I’m killing her control.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: No. A boy running out of air.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Ashfang’s guns are dead. Billie is launching.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Let her go—I’m losing the tug!

directionInline: Enter at maximum action with every visual system serving a human objective: Thunderbreak shields the habitat, Naomi holds the tug, Tess attacks the vent control, Paul crawls toward the valve, and Abby fights Ashfang. Billie tries to reduce Tess to Abby’s subordinate, but Tess returns the scene to the suffocating boy. The turn comes after Abby wins: destroy Billie’s pod or help Naomi keep the tug intact. Abby chooses rescue. Billie escapes, but the people live. Exit as air returns and former enemies pull one another upright.

Issue 2.summary: Auric survives without resolving its fractures: refugees gain a precarious home while every leader faces the political cost of saving them.
Issue 2.settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — CROWN RING OBSERVATION GALLERY — MORNING
panelPlan: Morning over Auric: the Crown Ring’s enormous cracked window frames a radiant planet and damaged ships; refugees and residents repair the gallery together.
Richard checks Paul’s frostbitten hands while he insists on returning to window watch; the Mother and Boy share breakfast with a Shard family.
Jex finds his once-secret passage copied on public repair slates; Halev receives notice that his coalition has withdrawn support.
Venn receives a tribunal summons as Naomi presents Halev with a civilian defense accord—Verge command, shared rescue obligations, no permanent Fleet base.
The Boy asks whether the gallery is home. His mother answers, ‘For tonight,’ as former enemies raise one transparent repair panel into the stars.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Civilian command, mutual rescue, no permanent Fleet base.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: And when the Fleet asks who authorized it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Tell them the person they relieved.

directionInline: Enter on survival as unfinished communal labor beneath Auric’s cracked window and the open universe. Each exchange carries a consequence forward—Richard and Paul’s changed bond, Jex’s lost monopoly, Halev’s collapsing coalition, Venn’s tribunal, and Naomi’s attempt to turn emergency cooperation into civilian power. The turn is Halev accepting an accord authorized by Auric rather than the Fleet. No conflict is falsely resolved. Exit on the Mother’s modest promise of one night and the Boy recognizing it as progress while former enemies repair the same view of the stars.

Issue 3.summary: Auric's opened luxury ring is shelter, not safety: refugees wake beneath chandeliers while longtime residents discover strangers occupying abandoned homes.
Issue 3.settingText: INT. AURIC BAZAAR — LUXURY RING CONCOURSE — MORNING
panelPlan: Wide chandelier concourse converted into a crowded shelter.
A resident confronts Richard at her sealed family apartment.
Paul moves protectively between the adults.
Halev arrives as Dain refuses an easy eviction.
Both families remain on opposite sides of one doorway.

dialogueInline.speaker: Resident
dialogueInline.text: My parents' things are still in there.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: We were told the rooms were empty.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: No one is being put outside.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: Then tell her where her parents go.

directionInline: Begin inside Issue Two's consequence. Nobody is a villain; rescue has become a conflict over home, and Halev's promise is exposed as incomplete.

Issue 3.summary: A shared heat failure forces two families into one room; Richard saves a resident child with medicine carried out of Tal Corvus.
Issue 3.settingText: INT. LUXURY RING — TEMPORARY APARTMENT
panelPlan: Emergency lights and visible breath crowd both families together.
The resident child collapses.
Richard opens his last field kit.
Paul steadies the lamp while the mother holds her child.
The child breathes as the adults meet eyes without reconciliation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Then tell me what she took.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Blue lips. Shallow breath. She isn't fine.

directionInline: Gratitude complicates the dispute without erasing it; medicine becomes relationship, not inventory.

Issue 3.summary: Venn leaves for tribunal; Naomi believes the Fleet is withdrawing its most trustworthy person exactly when Auric needs her.
Issue 3.settingText: INT. AURIC DOCK — DEPARTURE GLASS
panelPlan: Venn's escort shuttle waits beyond immense glass.
Naomi blocks Venn's path.
Their controlled anger closes the distance.
Venn almost reaches for Naomi and stops.
Venn boards while Naomi remains reflected beside the shuttle.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: They relieve you, and you still go when they call.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: If I refuse the hearing, Keating writes the reason for me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Then I say it where she can't bury it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Auric lives with what happened. You get to leave and explain it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Enough to wish you were wrong.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Come back with more than a wish.

directionInline: Respect and attraction live beneath a real political wound; avoid a sentimental farewell.

Issue 3.summary: Dominion frames Venn's tribunal as a clean command failure; Kerr forces the dead and saved back into the record.
Issue 3.settingText: INT. DAWNWARD HORIZON — ADMIRALTY TRIBUNAL — DAY
panelPlan: Venn stands alone below the circular Admiralty dais.
Keating projects Billie's escape and the damaged tug.
Dominion reduces the events to the order chain.
Kerr activates civilian testimony.
Venn faces accusation and survivors simultaneously.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Did you understand the withdrawal order?

dialogueInline.speaker: Keating
dialogueInline.text: And Billie Rusk escaped under your restraint.

dialogueInline.speaker: Keating
dialogueInline.text: Because restraint left her able to.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kerr
dialogueInline.text: The civilians are alive because Venn returned.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: This court is not weighing sentiment.

directionInline: Establish the institution's preferred narrow story and Venn's refusal to inhabit it.

Issue 3.summary: Richard discovers medical and infrastructure evidence that the Triarch manufactured the refugee crisis by cutting heat and medicine to disloyal districts.
Issue 3.settingText: INT. AURIC LUXURY RING — IMPROVISED CLINIC
panelPlan: Richard treats locals and refugees side by side.
He compares identical tissue damage across clinical records with district power and medicine shutdown logs.
Paul recognizes districts where official reports claimed unrelated shortages.
Tess sees the deliberate sequence in the timestamps.
Richard holds duplicated clinic and utility records as dangerous evidence, not a ceremonial archive object.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: No. They were turned off one at a time.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Clinic copies. Power logs. The official versions changed twice.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: If this leaves the room, they come for you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: They already came for everyone else.

directionInline: Evidence emerges through patients, clinical records, power logs and timestamps rather than archive mystique. Richard is not preserving names as ritual; he kept the working evidence because the official explanation did not match what happened to his patients.

Issue 3.summary: Halev asks Auric to extend shelter; Dain makes him admit that Verge families will pay for the promise.
Issue 3.settingText: INT. AURIC BAZAAR — CIVIC CHAMBER
panelPlan: The crowded chamber overlooks refugees beyond glass.
Halev asks for an extension.
Dain shows failing residential levels.
Wallace's market answer is rejected.
Naomi makes Halev name the harmed district.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: No one goes back to Tal Corvus.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: Another section lost heat last night.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Try pricing refugees out of shelter and I'll put you in an airlock.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: My district is sleeping six to a room.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: What do you want from me?

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: Tell them what we know before we tell them what we can do.

directionInline: Halev wants more shelter opened; Dain forces him to identify which already-crowded district will lose heat or space to make that possible.

Issue 3.summary: Families forced together refuse to reduce one another to abstractions when a local child needs refugee care.
Issue 3.settingText: INT. LUXURY RING — WARMING ROOM
panelPlan: Families pack around one improvised heater.
The resident child struggles to breathe.
Refugees surrender blanket and space.
Paul distracts the frightened children while Richard works.
The resident mother makes room for Richard.

dialogueInline.speaker: Boy
dialogueInline.text: Were these rooms always this cold?

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: No. They used to be ugly and warm.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Want to see a light trick?

directionInline: The families share blankets, heater space, and medical help despite visible distrust.

Issue 3.summary: Public knowledge of Jex's passage turns refuge into a hunted commodity; Tali warns him to close the remaining network.
Issue 3.settingText: INT. VEIL MARKET — JEX'S OFFICE / TALI'S SAFEHOUSE
panelPlan: Jex is surrounded by competing demands.
A private distorted-glass call resolves into Tali.
Her refuge quietly prepares to disappear.
Jex receives another plea from trapped families.
His hands hover between closing and accepting the route.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tali
dialogueInline.text: Three strangers asked for your passage by name.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Only three? Fame has been unkind.

directionInline: Tali is Jex's younger sister and moral equal, not hostage exposition.

Issue 3.summary: The Triarch offers peace if Auric returns Richard, forcing Paul to ask whether his surrender might save everyone else.
Issue 3.settingText: INT. IMPROVISED CLINIC — BROADCAST LIGHT
panelPlan: Clinic screens seize into a masked broadcast.
The Triarch promises restored trade and amnesty.
Richard is publicly labeled thief and traitor.
Paul studies his father while patients watch.
Richard kills the screen but cannot answer him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Triarch
dialogueInline.text: Return Richard Secundo. Reject Fleet occupation. Trade resumes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: If you go, do they leave Auric alone?

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Would you do it for me?

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: For you, I would do almost anything.

directionInline: Make the dilemma intimate; Richard cannot promise that refusal is harmless.

Issue 3.summary: Abby arrives alone with warning of Billie and Pike's gathering force; Auric must decide whether a disarmed Shard warlord may enter.
Issue 3.settingText: INT./EXT. AURIC SECURITY LOCK
panelPlan: Abby's tiny shuttle waits while Scythe remains distant.
She places her weapons in the lock tray.
Dain faces her through armored glass.
Abby shows Pike and Billie's gathering force.
Halev opens the door while Naomi remains ready.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Because Billie found captains who prefer revenge to survival.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: I want you alive enough to hate me tomorrow.

directionInline: Abby's public split already happened; this tests its cost and grants conditional access, not forgiveness.

Issue 3.summary: Abby expects Tess, her sister, to return; Tess refuses to abandon people harmed by captains they once led.
Issue 3.settingText: INT. AURIC LUXURY RING — CLINIC PASSAGE
panelPlan: The sisters see each other across the crowded clinic.
Abby offers Tess her command token.
Tess continues dressing a civilian wound.
Abby absorbs the refusal.
The token remains on an empty cot between them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Billie's gone. Pike chose her. Come home.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: My sister commanded people who did this.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: You think leaving me repairs it?

directionInline: The sisters cannot return to what they were; Tess means confession where Abby hears judgment.

Issue 3.summary: Kerr offers Venn a defensible lie; Venn insists the tribunal judge her actual rejection of Dominion's order.
Issue 3.settingText: INT. ADMIRALTY TRIBUNAL — RECESS ALCOVE
panelPlan: Venn and Kerr stand behind a translucent screen.
Kerr offers the prepared defense.
Venn deletes it.
Kerr warns her what honesty costs.
Venn returns without notes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kerr
dialogueInline.text: Say the return protected Fleet strategic interests.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kerr
dialogueInline.text: If you say it plainly, they'll use it against you before anyone else hears it.

directionInline: Kerr is trying to keep Venn from being stripped of command; Venn rejects the prepared defense and enters without notes.

Issue 3.summary: Keating freezes Fleet support to Auric, making Verge civilians bear part of the punishment for Venn's choice.
Issue 3.settingText: INT. AURIC ESCORT CONTROL / LUXURY RING
panelPlan: Naomi receives the withdrawal order.
Thunderbreak recedes beyond Auric jurisdiction.
The clinic loses a Fleet power feed.
Dain sees a shelter level go dark.
Naomi closes Venn's personal channel without calling.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Thunderbreak is ordered outside the boundary.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Commodore Venn no longer commands this ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: And we went dark while she spoke.

directionInline: As the withdrawal order lands, Thunderbreak moves beyond the boundary and the clinic loses Fleet power.

Issue 3.summary: Richard agrees to independent testimony only if his evidence cannot authorize Fleet occupation and Paul may remain private.
Issue 3.settingText: INT. AURIC ARCHIVE BOOTH — NIGHT
panelPlan: An independent evidence-and-broadcast booth waits dark.
Halev warns that a transmission from Auric makes the station a target.
Richard sets conditions limiting how his evidence may be used.
Paul refuses the seat beside him and Richard accepts the decision.
Dain activates the tamper-evident public feed and places Richard’s conditions at its beginning.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Broadcasting from Auric paints the station around you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: The target was painted before I arrived.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: Your conditions go into the record first.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: No Fleet custody. No occupation justified in my name.

directionInline: Father and son love each other without agreeing; Richard owns his evidence. Treat the booth as practical public-record infrastructure—camera, source files, provenance and tamper checks—not as a solemn archive space.

Issue 3.summary: Richard names individual victims; testimony spreads because it refuses strategic abstraction.
Issue 3.settingText: INT. AURIC ARCHIVE / INTERCUT TAL CORVUS
panelPlan: Richard sits alone before the camera with the source records available beside the feed.
An infant’s clinical entry is paired with the remembered face of the patient Richard actually treated.
A Shard engine crew stops work to listen.
Paul hears familiar people and districts named outside the booth.
Anonymous hands retransmit the testimony and supporting data before authorities can suppress the channel.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Nemi Vale. Six weeks old. Incubator power denied.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Ors Dane. Antibiotics withheld after his district protested.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Sergeant Pell carried medicine to children. They executed him for theft.

dialogueInline.speaker: Another Listener
dialogueInline.text: Send it before they cut the channel.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: They called them shortages. The logs show who was denied power and when.

directionInline: Each case links a specific person to a documented policy action and triggers someone else’s response. The power comes from evidence tied to human consequence, not ceremonial recitation of names.

Issue 3.summary: Billie accepts Pike's strike because Richard's truth makes Abby and Tess's rejection impossible to dismiss as weakness.
Issue 3.settingText: INT. BROKEN OATH — WAR ROOM
panelPlan: Richard's testimony fills the battered display.
A named child's death affects Billie.
Pike overlays the Auric attack path.
Billie sees the clinic marker.
She takes the strike control key.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: Now she chooses who governs the Shards.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: Abby ran. Tess hid behind bandages. The doctor makes it virtue.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: Then give her somewhere to stand.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: No. Make them watch her fail.

directionInline: Pike weaponizes Billie's personal wound; she knowingly escalates beyond Issue Two.

Issue 3.summary: Shard sleepers sabotage the luxury ring and plant Richard's insignia, turning residents against refugees as heat fails.
Issue 3.settingText: INT. LUXURY RING — HEAT EXCHANGE / CONCOURSE
panelPlan: A gloved hand destroys the exchanger and plants insignia.
Lights die across the concourse.
Residents find the planted evidence.
Accusation becomes a physical fight.
Richard places himself between Paul and the crowd.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Not by a badge left where you'd find it.

directionInline: Sabotage attacks social trust as much as infrastructure.

Issue 3.summary: Naomi forces Halev and Dain to tell everyone the ring may fail, choosing public trust over managed calm.
Issue 3.settingText: INT. AURIC CIVIC BROADCAST PLATFORM
panelPlan: The three argue while a crowd pounds the doors.
Halev asks for delay.
Dain demands evacuation.
Naomi activates the live feed mid-argument.
They face the frightened station together.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Say that now and people run.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: They're already running. They don't know where.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: The ring may not have one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: What we know and what we don't.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: The ring may not remain habitable.

directionInline: Truth causes fear but ends rumor-based violence and invites voluntary action.

Issue 3.summary: Halev and Dain surrender their own security before asking residents and refugees to share shelter.
Issue 3.settingText: INT. AURIC INNER SHELTER GATE
panelPlan: Officials privilege registered residents.
Richard turns away with Paul.
Halev tears up his own authorization.
Dain gives away her family berth.
Mixed families enter while both leaders remain outside.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: Where I was asking you to go.

directionInline: Leadership becomes costly and visible; capacity is not magically solved.

Issue 3.summary: Jex learns the public passage is watched; saving the ring requires exposing Tali's remaining private haven network.
Issue 3.settingText: INT. JEX'S OFFICE / TALI SAFEHOUSE / AURIC MAP
panelPlan: The public passage is surrounded by hostile contacts.
Naomi asks for another way.
Jex reveals a faint hidden web.
Tali understands his consideration.
Her haven glows as one node among many.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Your famous passage is a firing gallery.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: You're asking me to say that in front of the person who knows it isn't true.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tali
dialogueInline.text: They'll see everyone if you don't.

directionInline: End before the choice executes; Tali chooses with Jex rather than being passively sacrificed.

Issue 3.summary: Jex opens the private routes, saving the ring while Tali's refuge disappears from his board.
Issue 3.settingText: INT. JEX'S OFFICE / EXT. AURIC HIDDEN APERTURES
panelPlan: Jex releases the authentication web.
Concealed apertures ignite around Auric.
Civilian craft emerge toward the ring.
Tali's node flashes exposed.
It goes black under Jex's hand.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Once I send this, there are no private doors.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tali
dialogueInline.text: There are people behind the public ones.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: I can protect the ships. Not every origin.

directionInline: Make the hidden community wondrous and the loss immediate; Jex makes no bargain.

Issue 3.summary: Billie and Pike attack the evacuation; Billie drives toward Richard while civilians cross exposed spans.
Issue 3.settingText: EXT./INT. AURIC LUXURY RING — UNDER ATTACK
panelPlan: Pike's force erupts through fractured ring light.
Evacuation craft scatter.
Billie drives Ashfang into the structure.
The clinic ceiling tears as Tess shields Richard and Paul.
Billie sees the clinic marker ahead.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: It was split before we arrived.

directionInline: Escalation is deliberate and personal; civilians remain central to the spectacle.

Issue 3.summary: Naomi accepts Abby's ships only under Verge command and only to protect civilians.
Issue 3.settingText: INT. AURIC ESCORT CONTROL / ABBY'S SHUTTLE
panelPlan: Evacuation craft fill Naomi's displays.
Abby offers her remaining ships.
Naomi rejects broad command access.
She assigns civilian shield duty.
Abby relays the order to her defectors.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: I have six captains outside your line.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: They answer to me. They cover civilians. They do not pursue.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: You're putting me on a leash.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: I'm putting you between families and guns.
